<reason>Both sides argued at a high level, but CON won the clash that PRO itself designated as decisive. PRO defined "genuinely fair terms" to include an unpenalized, non-monitored option priced on ordinary actuarial factors, and CON immediately located the debate there and never let it move. CON's strongest sustained line — that the gap between monitored and unmonitored pools is not a "toll" but the loss truth about who is left, and that pricing an absent datum by average is ordinary practice (no-credit-score rate, untested-model rate) — survived contact. PRO's attempted debate-ender (CON concedes three of six fair terms, so the motion is basically granted) was met with a clean, principled distinction: supporting retention/purpose limits regardless of the motion is not agreeing to condition a pricing method on a legislated cross-subsidy. PRO gestured at that concession route but then chose to defend the disputed clause instead of cashing it, so the deflection held. CON's Pressure Q1 also extracted a real concession: PRO named the payer as monitored drivers via a shrunken discount, which CON converted into the memorable "transfer from the transparent to the opaque," reinforced in a vivid closing. PRO's best live ground — the ratchet in a state-compelled market, and the disanalogy that you can live without credit but cannot lawfully drive uninsured — remained genuinely alive and kept this competitive, but CON blunted it with "the price follows reality" plus the point that compulsion falls on the monitored driver too. Execution also mattered: PRO had three turns clipped for length, losing its closing lines in opening and both rebuttals, while CON stayed near-cap and intact. PRO's Q2 (granular indicator vs. coarse pool verdict) was the sharpest single question of the debate, but CON answered it directly and non-evasively.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Pressure Q1 forcing PRO to "name the payer," and the follow-up turn: once PRO conceded monitored drivers absorb the shortfall via a capped discount, CON reframed the motion as a legislated subsidy from the transparent to the opaque — a frame PRO never dislodged.</best_rebuttal>
